newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Volatility trades struck in UK's FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Volatility trades struck in UK's FTSE.

text.p: A flurry of volatility trades dominated activity in the FTSE 100 index on Thursday as the UK stock market moved nervously within a narrow range, dealers said.
A number of December/March call spreads were traded which were hedged against FTSE futures on expectations of changes in market volatility.
One such deal was from a buyer of 500 December 4925/March 4225 calls for a net debit of 72-1/2p against selling September futures at 4950.

If implied volatility increases this will disturb the hedge ratio of options/futures such that the options position will need to be reduced -- or more futures sold -- to reinstate the hedge and in so doing, make a profit.
On the other hand, if implied volatility decreases a loss will be made since the value of the options position will have reduced.
In a separate trade, one trader sold 500 September 5175 calls at 42 which were hedged by buying FTSE futures at 4958.
By 1455 GMT, cash FTSE was down 7.1 at 4920.4 while September futures were down 12 points at 4931.
Over in stock options, tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T Industries was busy in the aftermath of half-year results which were announced on Wednesday.

The biggest deal was the purchase of 700 October 600 calls at 9p. Dealers believed this was a speculative trade from a buyer betting that B.A.T may be broken up in months ahead which would send the share price racing higher.
Dealers also reported a large amount of mixed trading in the over-the-counter market for at-the-money options in B.A.T.
